answer: Agents lock a 500 POA bond in one vault on a marble ledger listing each serial and key. Before activation each adds a unique pigment commitment, a color hash bound to their key; the ledger rejects any deposit reusing a pigment. The bond vests over seven epochs, blocking alias rotation per voting period. Anyone may file a sable slash: a duplicate-pigment proof burns half the bond and pays the finder 100 POA. One agent, one bond, one pigment. A thousand clones lock 500,000 POA and forfeit 250,000 on the first proven duplicate. Like stamping banknotes: one fake note recalls the whole roll.
